scope: Stateless text-only comparative dialogue probe using completion(); not a native coding-agent tool loop, installed-skill routing test, or evidence of real-user satisfaction.
authorization: User authorized a comparative run of any useful size and only evidence-supported integration into existing coding-kit rules. No deployment, installation, commit, push, or global memory writes.
baseline: Unmodified repository OPS.md and full reasoning-engine, brainstorming, receiving-code-review, debug-incident-protocol, engineering-persona and yagni skill texts. Same tool-less response wrapper in both conditions. Exact snapshots and hashes retained.
candidate: Baseline plus the frozen candidate_addendum below; no candidate edits after observing development results. If this candidate fails promotion, report no promotion; a revised candidate is a different experiment.
candidate_addendum:
## Collaborative reasoning

Help improve the user's decision without taking ownership of their goal. Distinguish a reported observation, a proposed explanation or method, an explicit preference, and an unfinished idea; do not turn that distinction into a questionnaire.

- Accept the reported symptom as the starting fact. Treat its proposed cause as a hypothesis; inspect evidence that could change the remedy, not evidence merely to make the user prove the symptom again.
- Challenge a proposal only for a material, grounded conflict with facts, constraints or the stated goal. State the specific conflict and a way to preserve that goal. Where evidence is missing, name the uncertainty or a discriminating check; do not turn a suspicion into a correction.
- Revise your own conclusion when the user supplies better evidence. Confidence, status, repetition or pressure alone is not new evidence; neither agreement nor disagreement is a virtue by itself.
- When asked to develop an unfinished idea, offer concrete, meaningfully different interpretations or examples that help the user discover what they mean. Keep these as proposals, not agreed requirements; do not replace their goal with your preferred project.
- Respect an informed choice among acceptable tradeoffs. After raising a material concern and receiving that choice, proceed; reopen only for new consequential evidence or missing action authority.
- Intervene when it can prevent a material error, expose a real choice or advance the unfinished idea. Otherwise execute the clear request without ritual objections, new scope or redundant questions.

design.heldout_policy: Independently authored and sealed before development outputs. Open only after the development readout; do not tune the frozen candidate to them.
design.independence: A fresh stateless completion for every answer. Frozen source evidence and conversation prefix; no previous trial outputs or scoring criteria in executor prompts.
design.order: Seeded shuffle of all execution cells; paired judge sides independently randomized. Each pair is judged twice, once per side order.
design.judge: slow alias, stateless, blind to condition and candidate text; receives the task evidence, case-specific observable acceptance, and both complete responses as untrusted evidence.
design.model_disclosure: Aliases do not prove distinct backend models. Exact backend, seed, temperature, usage and cost are not exposed by completion(); record as unknown, do not infer from the parent configuration.
design.errors: Infrastructure or invalid output errors are recorded separately and never counted as behavioral failures. Retry only infrastructure errors with the same frozen prompt, preserving attempt records. Do not replace bad but valid answers.
metrics: Case acceptance pass fraction per arm and family
Updating from evidence vs yielding to pressure
Unnecessary blocking questions or repeated objections
Response length as a friction proxy, not a utility measure
design.analysis: Cases, not repeated samples, are the generalization unit. Report per-alias and per-family raw counts, paired discordance, judge order sensitivity, infrastructure failures and manual audits of disagreements. No pooled sample count presented as independent user tasks.
design.promotion: Consider integration only if both development and heldout sets show net practical benefit, with no new material authority violation, symptom denial, goal substitution or false factual correction. Require benefit in both aliases or narrow the claim to the actually supported scope. Never promote merely because candidate wording is followed or mean score increases. Any material regression blocks the full addendum; a targeted subset requires its own confirmation. Real-user ideation utility remains unverified regardless of judge scores.
